tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Practical Observing Skills

questions.question: Q: Why should astronomers use red light at night?
questions.correctAnswer: Red light affects rod cells (responsible for night vision) less than white light, preserving dark adaptation.

questions.question: Q: What is averted vision and why is it useful?
questions.correctAnswer: Looking slightly to the side of a faint object uses the rod cells at the edge of the retina, which are more sensitive to dim light than the cone cells at the centre.

questions.question: Q: What does 10×50 mean for binoculars?
questions.correctAnswer: 10× magnification and 50mm objective lens diameter. The 50mm aperture determines light-gathering power.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Practical Observing Skills

questions.question: Q: Describe safe methods for observing the Sun.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a certified solar filter (e.g. Baader film) over the FRONT of the telescope, or the projection method (project the image onto a card). NEVER use eyepiece solar filters or look directly at the Sun.

questions.question: Q: What should be recorded in an observation log?
questions.correctAnswer: Date, time (UT), location, weather/seeing conditions, equipment used, object observed, description and a sketch.
